study.title: Clinical-functional brain connectivity signature predicts longitudinal symptom improvement after acupuncture treatment in patients with functional dyspepsia
study.study_design: Prediction model development and validation study using retrospectively and prospectively gathered data from randomized controlled neuroimaging trials; machine learning-based prediction using clinical and resting-state fMRI features
study.randomization: Source trials were randomized controlled trials; the current prediction study aggregated samples across intervention groups
study.blinding: not_reported for the prediction study itself; source trials were randomized controlled
study.population: FD patients aged 18-40 years, right-handed, college degree or above
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) satisfied the Rome diagnostic criteria for FD; (2) were 18–40 years old; (3) were right-handed; (4) were a college degree or above; (5) did not get regulated treatment for at least 2 weeks prior to enrollment; (6) had not participated in any clinical trial in the last 3 months; (7) had signed the informed consent
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) had other organic or metabolic diseases which may induce dyspepsia symptoms; (2) had other functional gastrointestinal diseases such as irritable bowel syndrome; (3) had chronic pain disorders or mental disorders; (4) had a history of gastrointestinal surgery, head trauma, brain lesions, or neurological disorders; (5) were pregnant or planning to get pregnant in the last 6 months; (6) had any contraindication of Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scan

extraction_notes.note: Detailed acupuncture intervention parameters (needle type, size, depth, retention time, manipulation, deqi details) are stated to be available in Supplementary 1, which was not provided. Only the acupoints (ST36, BL21, CV12), session count (20), and duration (4 weeks) are extractable from the main text.
MRI scanning parameters (TR, TE, voxel size, scan duration, sequence details) are stated to be available in Supplementary 2, which was not provided.
Additional details on ICA and functional brain network construction are stated to be in Supplementary 3, which was not provided.
Spatial maps and detailed information on the 35 selected ICs are stated to be in Supplementary 4, which was not provided.

Detailed information on all 39 predictive features (including full rsFC feature identities, rsFC01-rsFC37) is stated to be in Supplementary 5, which was not provided. Only the top-5 weighted features and aggregate counts per region are extractable from the main text.

Detailed statistical results of two-sample t-tests for all 39 predictive features (Supplementary 6) were not provided. Only the directional summary (responders > nonresponders for 36/37 rsFC features) is available from the main text.
Deqi, pain, sensory, or interoceptive responses during acupuncture treatment were not assessed or reported in this study. No deqi measurement instrument is mentioned.
Expectancy, credibility, blinding success, and allocation guessing were not assessed or reported in this study. No such instruments are mentioned.
Adverse events were not mentioned or reported in the main text.
Ethics approval statement was not found in the main text.
Trial registration numbers for the source RCTs (Sun et al., 2018; Yin et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2022) are not reported in this paper.

The paper states patients received acupuncture stimulation at 'one or two acupoints' depending on group assignment in the source RCTs. Because samples from different intervention groups were aggregated, it is not possible to determine how many patients received each combination of acupoints. Detailed acupoint-by-group information is not provided in the main text.
The identity of rsFC31 (the one feature that did not show significant difference between responders and nonresponders) is not specified in the main text; it is presumably in Supplementary 5.

Exact network-scale weight values in Figure 2g are represented as dot sizes in a matrix and cannot be read precisely from the text or figure caption. The qualitative finding (CCN-CCN and CCN-DMN/SCN/SMN have largest weights) is reported in the text.

Full Circos diagram of 37 rsFC predictive features in Figure 2e shows all edges with their line thickness indicating weight, but individual edge identities and exact weights for all 37 features (rsFC01-rsFC37) are not readable from the main text; only the top-5 are explicitly named.

The training-test set was 'retrospectively gathered' from two source RCTs using Rome III criteria, while the independent validation set used Rome IV criteria. The paper states these are congruent but this may introduce heterogeneity.
Gender distribution differs substantially between training-test set (17M/72F) and independent validation set (24M/34F). The paper notes this may bias model performance in male patients.

The n_analyzed values (89 for training-test, 58 for validation) are inferred from the exclusion of 11 and 2 patients respectively due to head motion from the enrolled 100 and 60. These values are explicitly stated in the text.

No MNI coordinates are reported for any neural result in this paper. The neuroimaging analysis uses ICA-based network components and functional connectivity edges rather than voxelwise activation coordinates. No coordinate tables exist.
